plugin.name: Magic Tattoos Framework (core)
plugin.description:
Required.
Core engine: MTF ESL plugin, MCM, MTFPulse SKSE DLL, built-in conditions (magicka/stamina/combat/hits/time/etc.), built-in effects (drains, stagger, magic cost penalty, shaders, sounds, flashes, fades, transitions).
Hard requirements (you must have these installed first): - RaceMenu / SKEE (NiOverride) - PapyrusUtil SE - SKSE 64 - Skyrim SE 1.5.97 or Skyrim AE 1.6.x (CommonLibSSE-NG covers both)
This installer cannot auto-detect those because FOMOD only checks ESP/ESM files, not DLLs. If you don't have them, abort, install them, retry.
Also ships a skee64_custom.ini override that sets [Overlays] bPlayerOnly=0 so MTF can apply overlays to tracked NPCs. NiOverride only pre-allocates overlay slots on the player by default; flipping this allocates them on every humanoid actor. RAM use grows roughly proportional to the active NPC population — RaceMenu's stock ini warns "NOT RECOMMENDED" for this reason, but every NPC-tattoo mod (SlaveTats, etc.) requires it.
This uses RaceMenu's own skee64_custom.ini override mechanism: SKEE reads skee64.ini, then layers skee64_custom.ini on top per-section. It changes only this one key and does NOT conflict with or overwrite RaceMenu's ini, so load order relative to RaceMenu does not matter for it.

plugin.name: MTF Plugin: SlaveTats Bridge
plugin.description:
Bridges MTF tattoos into SlaveTats's per-actor state store so third-party mods that query SlaveTats (has_tattoo / query_applied_tattoos / has_applied_tattoos_with_attribute) see MTF tattoos as if they were applied via SlaveTats itself. Works for ALL pack roots, not just slavetats-prefixed ones.
Auto-recommended if SlaveTats.esp is active.
Requires JContainers SE (hard requirement of SlaveTats itself, so already present if you have SlaveTats installed).
Effect: slavetats.mirror — when bound to an MTF slot, ghost-writes the slot's tattoo into JFormDB so polling consumers see it.
How it stays safe for arbitrary pack roots: - synchronize_tattoos (SlaveTats's renderer) is guarded by an "updated" flag we never flip; in our normal flow it just doesn't run. - If something else does flip the flag, synchronize respects SlaveTats's own external_slots() detection: any slot whose NiOverride path doesn't start with "Actors\Character\slavetats\" is treated as externally owned and SlaveTats refuses to write or clear it. MTF paints first, so non-slavetats slots stay safely "external". - For slavetats-rooted packs (LewdMarks SlaveTats variant) the stored texture is prefix-stripped so any re-render reconstructs the same path MTF already painted (last-writer-wins on one slot, identical pixels). - upgrade_tattoos's wipe-on-first-touch is short-circuited by pre-setting .SlaveTats.version on the actor when we write our first ghost.
Use case: hook SlaveTats-aware mods (slavery mods, narrative mods) that treat tattoos as semantic state, without depending on those mods directly.

plugin.name: MTF Plugin: SkyrimNet Bridge
plugin.description:
Bridges MTF state to SkyrimNet so LLM-driven NPCs are aware of the player's currently visible tattoos and their effects.
Auto-recommended if SkyrimNet.esp is active.
What it does: - Adds a "Magic Tattoos" section to a character's SkyrimNet bio with a human-readable description of their current tattoo + active effects, so the AI knows what's on their skin. - Listens for MTF_TierChanged and fires SkyrimNetApi.RegisterShortLivedEvent (30s TTL, deduped) so a tier swap shows up in scene context for the next LLM call. - Ships a prompt submodule (SKSE/Plugins/SkyrimNet/prompts/submodules/character_bio/0350_mtf_tattoos.prompt) that renders the bio block as the "Magic Tattoos" section in character bios.
Scope (v0.1.20): - Player-only narration. NPC preset tier changes are also broadcast by MTF's universal events, but the bridge ignores them — SkyrimNet's scene-context routing is player-centric. - Pack/entry/effect descriptions come from the optional `description` fields authored on plugin scripts (effects, conditions) and pack JSONs (entry visuals). Missing fields fall back to the short MCM label so installations without authored prose still produce usable output.
Use case: have NPCs react to tattoos in dialogue without writing per-mod glue or YAML triggers.

plugin.name: Test Pack (smoke-test presets + F10 console runner)
plugin.description:
Bundles MTF's smoke-test infrastructure:
- 33 smoke-test preset JSONs (Test_*.json). Drive the framework into specific code paths from the MCM Presets dropdown.
- MTF_TestRunner.pex — ReferenceAlias script that binds to the MTF_TestRunner alias already declared on MTF_MainQuest. Exposes a console-callable test suite (e.g. F10 in-game macro running `cqf MTF_MainQuest RunTests`) covering the base plugin's conditions / effects under an AAA pattern.
Hard requirement for the runner: ConsoleUtilSSE NG (for coc teleport in location-based tests). The presets work without it; only the console-callable suite needs it.
For development / verification use. Safe to skip if you don't intend to run the test scenarios documented in TEST_METHODOLOGY.md.

plugin.name: Example preset: Magicka Tracker
plugin.description:
A ready-made example preset that turns one Body tattoo into a live magicka gauge:
- Full magicka -> calm violet tattoo (Sanguine Back), gentle pulse - below 70% -> amber, brighter glow - below 40% -> crimson, fast urgent pulse - below 10% -> tattoo hidden ("burned out")
Load it from the MCM Presets dropdown ("Magicka Tracker"), then apply via the spell or alias. A good worked example of slot priority, magicka.below thresholds, inherited textures, and pulse — documented in docs/MCM_OPTIONS.md.
Requires the Bitchcraft content pack (this FOMOD's Content step) for the texture it points at. Without it the preset loads but renders nothing until you repoint its Default slot to any Body pack in the MCM.

plugin.name: SPID NPC Distribution (requires SPID)
plugin.description:
Auto-applies MTF presets to NPCs by rule, the way SPID distributes spells/items. The mapping is MTF-owned JSON; SPID is only the per-NPC trigger (a self-deleting ability), so installing this is the only thing that pulls in a SPID dependency — core MTF never needs it.
Ships: - MTF_SPID_Distributor_DISTR.ini — distributes the "MTF Distribute" carrier ability to NPCs (edit its SPID filters to taste). - distribution/sample.json — a sample rule (Lydia -> 50/50 between two presets). Edit/replace with your own rules.
Rule filters: specific npcs, keywords (+ exclude), factions, races, formlists, sex, level range, chance, and weighted preset lists (one of N at given odds).
REQUIRES: Spell Perk Item Distributor (SPID) — install separately. The sample targets Lydia with test-pack presets; repoint it at your own presets/NPCs.
